findings.evidence: "The arrowhead sits on the side it is written" introduces a standard UML relationship table. Alongside the basic shape-role inventory in authoring-rules.md and link inventory in flowcharts.md, these sections spend context on familiar syntax rather than the stronger parser, renderer and silent-failure knowledge elsewhere.
findings.fix: Reduce the standard relationship table to a brief orientation reminder, and shorten the basic shape/link inventories and routine example members. Retain the Mermaid-specific generics, multiplicity parsing, identifier and renderer traps.

findings.evidence: "Six or more nodes with no `classDef` read as flat default gray: give them a palette" makes styling mandatory by node count; line 111 further requires "Otherwise copy one block below; do not invent hex colors." These rigid aesthetic constraints also apply when the host theme already communicates the diagram adequately.
findings.fix: Make the node-count threshold and bundled palettes defaults rather than requirements. Permit host-themed diagrams and other accessible palettes when they suit the audience; retain strict contrast requirements whenever custom colors are used.

findings.evidence: The orders-erd assertion only requires "Shows order-line and item-product cardinalities" although the prompt says "include keys." An ERD with missing PK/FK annotations or incorrect cardinalities could satisfy the listed checks.
findings.fix: Add assertions for PK/FK annotations, exactly one order and one product per line item, the corresponding many-side endpoints, and explicit assumptions where minimum child counts are unspecified.

findings.evidence: The repair branch says "change only syntax" and "read the type file only if the parse error is not covered there." A syntactically valid but inverted class relationship never satisfies that loading condition, even though class-diagrams.md explicitly documents this silent failure.
findings.fix: Separate parse-only repair from semantic or rendering repair. For incorrect arrows, missing elements or other silent failures, load the matching type reference even when parsing succeeds, and permit corrections that restore the user-intended meaning. Keep syntax-only preservation for requests limited to parse repair.

findings.evidence: Links: `-->`, `---` (no arrow), `-.->` (dotted), `==>` (thick), `-->|label|`; `A --> B & C` fans out.
findings.fix: Delete the basic link and shape syntax list, which the model already knows. Keep only the `A(Text)` vs `A([Text])` confusion and the `linkStyle` index-shift trap.

findings.evidence: | `->>` / `-->>` | Sync call / dashed reply | ... | `->` / `-->` | Plain line, no arrowhead |
findings.fix: Trim the arrow table to the non-obvious rows (`-)` async and `-x` lost), since the model knows the standard arrows.

Put the repair-or-new fork before the read step and say which sections each path reads. SKILL.md would then show the routing as a clear decision tree. Most of the thinking framework (choose by question answered) lives only in authoring-rules.md section 1; add one line to SKILL.md naming it.

findings.evidence: The only pitfall in SKILL.md is `## C4 pitfall`. The other silent failures sit in the type files (for example `## Silent failures` in erd-diagrams.md).
findings.fix: Add a short `## Gotchas` or NEVER list to SKILL.md with the highest-cost silent failures and a pointer to each type file. Candidates: the inverted class arrow, a gantt date that does not match dateFormat, the gitGraph `checkout` before `branch`, and the subgraph `direction` being ignored. The agent often will not recognize the trigger to open the right type file.

findings.evidence: Picks among sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, C4, stateDiagram-v2, flowchart, architecture-beta, gantt, pie and gitGraph.
findings.fix: Replace the description with: "Create, edit, and repair Mermaid diagrams (.mmd files or ```mermaid blocks in Markdown). Use this skill when users ask to diagram, visualize, model, map out, or show sequence diagrams, class diagrams, ER diagrams or database schemas, state machines, flowcharts, software architecture (including terse requests such as 'architecture: mobile client, API, database, email provider'), Gantt schedules, pie proportions, or Git branch history, or when a Mermaid diagram fails to render or export (mmdc, GitHub), even without naming Mermaid. Choose the diagram type from the question being answered: sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, C4, stateDiagram-v2, architecture-beta, gantt, pie, gitGraph, with flowchart as the last resort. Not for prose-only explanations, explaining an existing diagram without changing it, PlantUML or draw.io work, matplotlib data charts, or interactive diagram-canvas components."

findings.evidence: Mandatory read for every new diagram, including sections 4-6 (subgraphs, shapes, classDef palettes), which the file itself labels flowchart-only.
findings.fix: Move the flowchart-only sections 4-6 into `flowcharts.md`, or tell the agent to read them only for a flowchart. A sequence or ERD diagram would then not load them.
Keep one default pack example and cut the list of alternative packs. This section is already gated to renderers known to register the pack, so a menu adds no value.

findings.evidence: The 12 evals cover type choice, repair, C4 duplicate ids, gantt, gitGraph and prose-only. None asserts the authoring-rules styling or layout rules: classDef contrast, subgraph direction, 900px proportion, or splitting a large diagram.
findings.fix: Add an eval for a flowchart of about 12 nodes. Its assertions should check that `classDef` sets fill, stroke and color together, that the diagram is TD, that no cross-boundary edge sits beside a subgraph `direction`, and that the diagram is split if it is oversized. Add a repair eval for a lowercase `end` in a sequence diagram.

findings.evidence: Repair: ... Check authoring-rules.md section 7 first and read the type file only if the parse error is not covered there. Skip the layout and styling rules. (vs step 2: "Read authoring-rules.md before drawing (mandatory)")
findings.fix: Reconcile steps 2 and 3. Say that a repair reads only authoring-rules.md section 7, and that the full read applies to new diagrams only. The mandatory-read line currently contradicts the repair shortcut.

findings.evidence: README tells readers to see "Classify before you draw" in SKILL.md and to validate in Mermaid Live. SKILL.md has no such section and requires mmdc validation.
findings.fix: Update the README pointers to match the current SKILL.md and mmdc validation step. The README stays as the repo-required file.
